> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `6bfb7adf8213fe55d7617abdf033502e8ae72916` — the merge of head `e747839220be43ed47f475df379e33bc482f340f` into base `b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6bfb7adf8213fe55d7617abdf033502e8ae72916 && git checkout 6bfb7adf8213fe55d7617abdf033502e8ae72916
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 e747839220be43ed47f475df379e33bc482f340f && git checkout -B drift-repro b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 && git merge --no-ff e747839220be43ed47f475df379e33bc482f340f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e747839220be43ed47f475df379e33bc482f340f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md + packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.ts, docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md, skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md, skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, packages/skills/package.json, packages/skills/scripts/sync-catalog.mjs, .changeset/config.json

The rest of the diff — the changeset file and the three regenerated reference pages under `content/docs/references/**` — is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files. Read against `origin/main` `b6e870707` (the PR's current base) and the PR's net diff against `main` at the head; the card (#25129, every comment) and ruling record 6308445871 (#24981, letter A) read in full. Inputs were the brief's list and nothing else; the dispatching seat's conclusions were not taken as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`titleFormat` describe, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:2844` — RIGHT.** A `.describe()` string only; the key stays `TemplateExpressionInputSchema.optional()`, deprecated, render-only, `nameField` precedence unchanged. The new prescription is the ruling's item 2 shape and matches, word for word in substance, the two places PR #25127 already landed it: ADR-0079 D3 (`docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md:140-148`, "a composite title that must be queried (matched by an import, sorted, searched) becomes a stored computed field (a non-formula field with an `expression`, written on write), designated as the `nameField` … a `formula` field with `returnType: 'text'` … stays legal for a title shown for display only") and the enforcing lint `packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.ts:80-88` and `:103-106` (`title-format-retired` message and hint: "a composite title that import, sort or search must match is a stored field with an expression designated nameField (a formula title is for display only)"). Rule and gate now say one thing. The four regenerated rows (object, metadata, migration x2) carry the identical sentence; `check:docs` runs in `Type Check · source gates`, green on the head.
   - The claim "computed and stored on every write" is real on `main`: `planStoredExpressions` (`engine.ts:3030-3058`) plans every non-`formula` field declaring an `expression`; the insert path computes over the FINAL rows after hooks and strips (`engine.ts:16925-16960`); update by id computes over the stored row merged with the patch and `applyStoredExpressionsToPatch` writes it (`:18650-18670`, `:3138-3146`); a predicate update computes before/after images and `settleBulkStoredExpressions` (`:3102-3131`) deletes the caller's key, stores one uniform value when an input moved, refuses on divergence. Consistent with the `FieldSchema.expression` describe (`field.zod.ts:1856`). One elision, not a defect: a predicate update that moves no input recomputes nothing — the stored value is then still the expression over the stored row, so the prescription holds.
   - A stored computed field is a legal `nameField`: an explicit pointer is honoured whatever the field's eligibility (ADR-0079 D4; `display-name.ts:resolveDisplayField`), and a `text` field carrying an `expression` is title-eligible by type anyway (`TITLE_ELIGIBLE_TYPES`, `display-name.ts:102-130`). No lint refuses the shape the describe now prescribes.

2. **`nameField` describe and TSDoc left alone (`object.zod.ts:2826-2836`) — RIGHT.** The describe prescribes nothing for a composite title; the TSDoc's "(text / autonumber / formula→text)" is D1's wording, which the ADR-0079 addendum qualifies in place without editing (`0079:404-407`: "D1 lists a text `formula` among the 'real STORED' title fields. It is a declared field of the object, but no column holds its value"). Inside the dispatch's conditional ("if it carries the same prescription"); no surface change.

3. **SKILL.md `nameField` row — RIGHT.** Same shape as the lint hint and the ruling. "a text formula is display-only" is ADR-0079 addendum item 9 (sort refused `400 INVALID_SORT`, search cannot reach it) plus ruling item 1 (a formula-titled import target keeps answering `reference_not_found`). The package stays self-consistent: `references/data-hooks.md:369` ("`ctx.title()` resolves this object's `nameField`, a **formula** included") is a display read, which item 9 leaves legal.

4. **SKILL.md `titleFormat` row — RIGHT.** "a composite title follows the `nameField` row" delegates to the row two lines above it; one prescription in the file, nothing left to drift.

5. **`rules/relationships.md` "Computed column" bullet — RIGHT, and the deleted text was a live contradiction with `main`.** The old bullet ("the server only treats `type: 'formula'` as computed, so on a stored field the `expression` is a client compute hint and the sent value is stored verbatim") is the opposite of the engine: `engine.ts:3030-3040` says verbatim "A client-sent value never stands: it is overwritten by the computed one"; under `strictReadonlyWrites` such a write is REFUSED and nothing is written (`stored_expression`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts:126-135`), and a non-strict write is completed with the computed value and reported through `onFieldsDropped`. The bullet's surviving half ("Keep it stored (NOT a `formula` field) so the parent `summary` can roll it up") agrees with `field.zod.ts:1856`. Seat pointer 6333459023 discharged.

6. **The three deletions that paid the SKILL.md token ceiling — each judged for load-bearing content and reachability, all RIGHT:**
   - "It used to clear both and then never match." (`SKILL.md:158`): incident narrative; the rule it trailed survives whole in the same paragraph (refused, not silent; `searchable-field-unsearchable` at `os validate`; `400 INVALID_FIELD` at request time). Not load-bearing for an author; the history remains for doc readers at `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx:152`.
   - "(Reminder: two consecutive `os build` runs with no source change must be byte-identical — see the determinism gate above.)" (`SKILL.md:458-459`): the pointer was dangling — nothing above it in SKILL.md states a determinism gate. The gate lives in the same package at `references/seeds.md:129-130` ("Determinism gate: two consecutive `os build` runs with no source changes must produce byte-identical `dist/objectstack.json`"), reachable from `SKILL.md:434`'s link to `references/seeds.md`, and is restated in `evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json:37`. Information still reachable; a wrong cross-reference removed.
   - The doubled `---` separator (`SKILL.md:392-394`): cosmetic.
   - Token readings reproduced from the head files' bytes (a read of the blobs, not a run): `SKILL.md` 24413 bytes minus the 20-byte `version:` stamp line gives ceil(24393 / 4) = 6099 against ceiling 6123 (`check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:404`); `rules/relationships.md` 14687 bytes gives 3672 against 3676 (`:534`). The diff touches no ceiling row. Net lines: SKILL.md 469 to 465, relationships.md 401 to 401. The ratchet and its self-test run in `Type Check · source gates` (`lint.yml:5636-5641`), green on the head; so do `check:skill-refs`, `check:skill-frame-sync`, `check:skill-compatibility`, `check:skill-top-level-keys`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`.

7. **Reconciliation ledger note, `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts:404` — RIGHT.** `why` is free prose asserted only for a length longer than 20 characters (`:996`, `:1092`); the new text quotes the new describe faithfully, and "every target is authorable" stays true (`nameField` is authorable; a non-formula field with an `expression` is authorable).

8. **Published-surface inventory.** `@objectstack/spec`: one JSON-schema `description` moves, no key, type, default, accepted value or export (`check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` green). `@objectstack/skills`: ships `skills/**` byte for byte (`packages/skills/scripts/sync-catalog.mjs`; `files: ["dist", …]`, `publishConfig.access: public`), so the skill text change publishes; `gen:skill-docs` reads frontmatter only (`packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts` header), untouched here. No runtime path changes anywhere in the diff.

9. **Sweep, my own on `origin/main` `b6e870707`.** `skills/**`: "composite" with formula / title / nameField hits only the two SKILL.md rows; `returnType: 'text'` only those two; "stored verbatim" / "compute hint" only the relationships.md bullet. `packages/spec/src/**`: the describe and the ledger note only. Hand-written docs the Docs Drift bot named: `formulas.mdx:99` already carries the new shape (from #25127); `objects.mdx:70` and `schema-design.mdx:59` describe `titleFormat` as deprecated render-only with no migration prescription — nothing to re-word. The dev's H2 and H3 hold.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25129-composite-title-stored-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `patch` and `@objectstack/skills` `patch` — RIGHT. Both are released packages the diff moves, both in the changeset `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`). Nothing an author can write changes, so `Metadata-protocol: none` and the level `none` takes is `patch`; the accepted set neither widens nor narrows, so `Clause-②: no` with no arm. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and the two agree. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong: the skill text ships in the `@objectstack/skills` tarball. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `Check Changeset` green on the head.

Clause-②: no

`out_of_scope_findings`, both "noted, not filed", both accepted under Prime Directive #10 (neither is a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap): (a) the `nameField` TSDoc lists `formula→text` among stored title fields — a source comment the ADR-0079 addendum already qualifies in place; (b) `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` entries (release-owned) and two test docblocks describe landed migrations as history, not as prescriptions.

The five required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and its six shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (two runs, both green).
